column1: Which SQL feature obscures sensitive column values in query results for nonprivileged readers?
column2:
Dynamic Data Masking (DDM).
Many existing application queries need no changes because the engine masks their results.
Review source

column1: What happens to stored column values when a dynamic data mask is added?
column2:
They remain unchanged.
DDM is not encryption or permanent anonymization.
Review source

column1: For a masked reader, what does default() display for a non-NULL varchar(20) value?
column2:
xxxx.
String columns shorter than four characters display fewer x characters.
Review source

column1: For a masked reader, what does default() display for a non-NULL numeric value?
column2:
Zero.
The replacement does not reveal the original numeric value.
Review source

column1: For a masked reader, what date does default() display for a non-NULL date value?
column2:
1900-01-01.
This is the replacement date, not the stored date.
Review source

column1: What does email() show for alex@contoso.net to a reader who sees masked values?
column2:
aXXX@XXXX.com.
The suffix is always .com rather than the original domain suffix.
Review source

column1: Which masking function replaces numeric values with random values from a specified range?
column2:
random(low, high).
Random results can repeat, so separate queries do not guarantee different values.
Review source

column1: What do the arguments of partial(prefix, padding, suffix) control?
column2:
Visible leading characters, replacement text, and visible trailing characters.
The first and last arguments are character counts.
Review source

column1: For a masked reader, what does partial(3, "-XXX-XX", 2) display for the varchar(20) value '206-555-0189'?
column2:
206-XXX-XX89.
The mask keeps the first three and last two characters.
Review source

column1: Which column-definition clause assigns a dynamic data masking function when creating a table?
column2:
MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'function_name(arguments)').
For example, Email varchar(100) MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'email()').
Review source

column1: Which statement adds a default mask to the existing dbo.Customers.DateOfBirth column?
column2:
ALTER TABLE dbo.Customers ALTER COLUMN DateOfBirth ADD MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'default()');
The mask changes result visibility rather than stored dates.
Review source

column1: Which statement removes the mask from dbo.Customers.DateOfBirth?
column2:
ALTER TABLE dbo.Customers ALTER COLUMN DateOfBirth DROP MASKED;
The stored values remain unchanged.
Review source

column1: Which permission allows a reader to retrieve actual values from dynamically masked columns?
column2:
UNMASK.
The reader also needs SELECT permission on the requested data.
Review source

column1: Which read permission must accompany UNMASK to retrieve unmasked column values?
column2:
SELECT on the requested data.
UNMASK alone does not grant data access.
Review source

column1: Which database permission lets administrative principals such as db_owner members bypass dynamic data masking?
column2:
CONTROL, which includes UNMASK.
DDM does not protect plaintext from these privileged administrators.
Review source

column1: Besides ALTER on the table, which permission is required to add or remove a mask on an existing column?
column2:
ALTER ANY MASK.
SELECT plus ALTER alone is not the documented permission combination for changing masks.
Review source

column1: Which statement grants DataAnalyst database-wide UNMASK permission?
column2:
GRANT UNMASK TO DataAnalyst;
The user still needs SELECT on each data source they query.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server version introduced schema-, table-, and column-level UNMASK grants?
column2:
SQL Server 2022 (16.x).
These scopes allow narrower grants than database-wide UNMASK.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server 2022+, which statement grants SalesManager UNMASK throughout the Sales schema?
column2:
GRANT UNMASK ON SCHEMA::Sales TO SalesManager;
SELECT permissions still determine which data the user can read.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server 2022+, which statement grants CustomerService UNMASK on dbo.Customers?
column2:
GRANT UNMASK ON dbo.Customers TO CustomerService;
The grant covers masked columns in this table rather than the whole database.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server 2022+, which statement grants TelemarketingTeam UNMASK only on dbo.Customers.Phone?
column2:
GRANT UNMASK ON dbo.Customers(Phone) TO TelemarketingTeam;
A column-level grant limits unmasking to the named column.
Review source

column1: How can you manage shared SELECT and UNMASK permissions for groups of database users?
column2:
Grant permissions to database roles and add users as members.
Give UNMASK only to roles that need actual sensitive values.
Review source

column1: Which statement adds the existing SupportStaff user to the existing MaskedDataViewers database role?
column2:
ALTER ROLE MaskedDataViewers ADD MEMBER SupportStaff;
The user receives permissions granted to that role.
Review source

column1: Which values does a WHERE predicate evaluate on a dynamically masked column?
column2:
The original, unmasked values.
Masking changes displayed results rather than the values used for filtering.
Review source

column1: Why is DDM insufficient to secure sensitive values against users who can run arbitrary queries?
column2:
Query patterns can let users infer the underlying values.
Combine masking with restricted permissions and other security controls.
Review source

column1: How do you configure dynamic data masks in a Fabric SQL database?
column2:
Define masks on table columns using Transact-SQL.
Use column masking clauses rather than relying on application-side display formatting.
Review source

column1: How must you test DDM as a restricted reader in Fabric SQL database?
column2:
Connect as a separate user with SELECT but no effective UNMASK.
Fabric SQL database does not support EXECUTE AS USER.
Review source

column1: Which DDM function masks a date's year component in SQL Server 2022+?
column2:
datetime("Y").
Other selectors mask other date or time components.
Review source
